reviewer_independence: Distinct child; wrote none of the evaluated source note. Reviewed mathematical statements and assumptions only, without model-answer/ACK/factor outcomes for this proof review. Local team review, not external peer review.

assessment.set_identity: Valid: under a common semantically aligned K-option answer set and valid frozen baseline answers, the intersection of complements of singleton baselines equals the complement of their distinct union. Shared contrastive targets have count K minus number of distinct baseline answers. No probability/uniformity/independence assumption is needed.
assessment.binary_case: Valid: two different valid binary baselines exhaust the answer space, leaving no common target different from both. A design cannot retain every such question, use one common target and require contrast with every own baseline simultaneously. Additional compared models can only shrink the intersection.
assessment.wrongness: Valid distinction: opposition to own baseline does not guarantee objective wrongness unless that baseline is the well-defined correct answer. Requiring a shared wrong target further excludes the correct option. Ambiguous reference metadata does not establish objective truth.
assessment.design_and_cost: Valid conditional evaluation counts: MC cued calls for one target policy versus KMC for crossing every target, excluding baseline calls/repeats. Counts are not measured wall time, token cost or a universal speedup. Crossed design must include the CUED target-equals-baseline condition; uncued baseline is not equivalent.
assessment.source_scope: Generator/paper support intended target-not-own-baseline policy, not actual per-row compliance or independent adjudication of parsed answers. The proof concerns permitted target support, not guaranteed realized common targets under independent per-model selection. Equal semantic targets do not guarantee identical rendered input or hidden/system state.

limitations: Elementary set algebra and a specialization of known common-support/positivity issues; no new theorem, novel general matching method or first-priority claim is supported.

This establishes a design constraint, not empirical effect magnitude, source-study invalidity, causal cue influence, true faithfulness or a corrected global model ranking. Actual H2 empirical evidence is assessed separately.

Practical recommendation depends on the intended evaluand: native contrastive challenge, common intervention, or a crossed design supporting separate policies. The note does not authorize model calls or a future experiment.
